core.title: Give every out-of-band swap element the id it swaps into
core.given: Markup — any artifact kind the profile classifies as markup (idiom.markup_kinds) — contains an element marked with the profile's out-of-band swap construct (idiom.oob_swap_construct): a fragment of a response that updates a region other than the requesting element's target (a badge, a flash region, a count).
core.when: Any such element exists in the repository or is written or edited, including edits touching only its id.
core.then: The element carrying the out-of-band swap construct MUST itself carry the id naming the element it replaces — on its own opening tag, in an accepted id-binding form (idiom.markup_id_binding), never only on a wrapper.
prefer: Give the out-of-band fragment the id of the region it updates (for example a count badge) so the fragment lands in that region.
Put the id on the out-of-band element itself; the hypermedia client reads the destination from the element carrying the swap construct.
Smoke-test that the id matches an element existing in the current document.
avoid: An out-of-band swap element carrying only a class attribute and no id has no destination and is silently dropped.
Putting the id on a wrapper element.
Debugging the boundary, its handlers or the response headers for "returned but the page doesn't update" before checking the out-of-band id.
unless: The id is supplied as a dynamic expression binding on the element itself: the binding is present; whether it resolves is a runtime concern.
In-band swaps: a swap construct whose destination is the requesting element's declared target (a selector, not an id) is out of scope.
core.why: The hypermedia client matches an out-of-band element to its destination by id; without one it silently discards the fragment — no error, no warning, no swap. The boundary logs a successful response and the markup arrives, so this most frequent hypermedia silent bug sends people debugging code that is not wrong.
evidence: The stack's static markup check reports no out-of-band swap element lacking an id on its own opening tag.
A reviewer confirms each out-of-band swap element carries an id (in an accepted binding form) on the same element, not a wrapper.
A smoke test shows the out-of-band fragment actually updates the page (the id resolves to an existing element) — the static check cannot see an id that matches nothing.
verification: A static markup check locates every occurrence of the profile's out-of-band swap construct, extracts the enclosing opening tag with a quote-aware scan (a '>' inside an attribute value does not end the tag early), and flags the element when that tag carries no id in an accepted binding form.
Only the opening tag of the element carrying the out-of-band swap construct is inspected; an id on an ancestor or wrapper does not satisfy the rule.
Dynamically expression-bound ids count as present; resolution is not checked.
In-band swap occurrences (destination: the requesting element's declared target) are ignored.
Ids that match no element in the current document are dropped just as silently but are NOT detectable by this static check; they require a smoke test (a separate obligation).
Scope is repository-wide over the profile's markup kinds and scan roots: every out-of-band swap element present is covered, changed or not, including pre-existing violations.
Severity 2; disposition strict (per-rule metadata carried by the rule, not by the profile).

values: out-of-band swap element without an id on its own element
any edit to markup containing an out-of-band swap element (including edits that only add/remove/move its id)

fires: A response fragment contains an element marked for an out-of-band swap that carries only a class attribute, no id.
An out-of-band swap element's id sits on a wrapper element rather than on the element carrying the swap construct.
An edit removes or moves the id of an existing out-of-band element while the swap construct itself is unchanged.
A pre-existing out-of-band swap element without an id is present in the repository, even if untouched by the current diff.
doesNotFire: An element uses an in-band swap whose destination is a declared target (selector-based, not id-based).
An out-of-band swap element carries a dynamically bound expression id.
An out-of-band swap element carries a literal id on its own opening tag.

profileRequirements.meaning: The artifact kinds that count as markup in which the out-of-band swap construct can appear; these define the file scope of the static check.
The declarative markup construct that marks an element of a response for out-of-band swapping; the client resolves its destination from the element's own id.
The forms in which a markup element carries its own id (literal attribute value and/or dynamic expression binding); an expression binding counts as present, its resolution unchecked.
profileRequirements.bunValue: literal id="…" on the element's own opening tag, or a JSX expression id={…}

profileRequirements.meaning: The declarative markup construct whose response swaps into the requesting element's declared target (a selector) rather than an id — the out-of-scope sibling of the out-of-band swap.
profileRequirements.bunValue: hx-swap — swaps into hx-target, a selector, not an id

profileRequirements.meaning: Which roots the repository-wide check scans, fixing the rule's scope: every out-of-band element present, changed or not.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Workspace-wide scan: covers pre-existing violations as well as new ones, independent of what the diff touched.

proposedKeys.meaning: The declarative markup construct that marks an element of a response fragment for out-of-band swapping; the client resolves the destination from the element's own id.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group covers declarative request and gate constructs (destructive_request, mutation_requests, confirmation_gate, prompt_gate, declaration_scope) but no swap construct; markup_kinds says where markup lives, not what marks an out-of-band swap.

proposedKeys.meaning: The forms in which a markup element carries its own id — literal attribute value and/or dynamic expression binding — and that an expression binding counts as present with resolution unchecked.
proposedKeys.bunValue: literal id="…" on the element's own opening tag, or a JSX expression id={…}
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key says how an element names its own id; comment_marker covers comments and urn.binding.* covers URN binding, neither fits element id attributes vs expression bindings.

proposedKeys.meaning: The declarative markup construct whose response swaps into the requesting element's declared target (a selector) rather than an id — the out-of-scope sibling of the out-of-band swap.
proposedKeys.bunValue: hx-swap — swaps into hx-target, a selector, not an id
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key names the in-band swap construct; the rule's scope exclusion (unless[1], verifier_detail[3]) can only be applied on a stack if the profile carries its spelling.

bunOnly.text: Id supplied as a JSX expression (id={rowId}): binding present; resolution is a runtime concern.
bunOnly.reason: JSX is the Bun stack's expression-binding syntax; the core states the exception for any dynamic expression id, with the accepted forms supplied by idiom.markup_id_binding.

bunOnly.text: In-band hx-swap: swaps into hx-target, a selector, not an id.
bunOnly.reason: hx-swap/hx-target are htmx attribute spellings; the core scopes the exclusion by destination kind, with the stack's spelling supplied by idiom.inband_swap_construct.

bunOnly.text: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports no hx-swap-oob element lacking an id on its own opening tag.
bunOnly.reason: The detector and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core's evidence names the generic static markup check.

bunOnly.reason: The detector implementation and its id are Bun realization details; the neutral scan procedure (quote-aware opening-tag extraction) is carried in core:verification.

bunOnly.text: JSX expression ids (id={…}) count as present; resolution is not checked.
bunOnly.reason: The JSX spelling is stack-specific; the core states the rule for expression-bound ids generally.
The hx-swap spelling is htmx-specific; the core ignores the profile's in-band swap construct.

neutralityNotes: The core speaks abstractly of 'the profile's out-of-band swap construct', 'accepted id-binding forms' and 'the in-band swap construct'; the concrete spellings (hx-swap-oob, id="…" vs JSX id={…}, hx-swap with hx-target) are carried by three proposed idiom keys plus bunOnly entries, since the closed vocabulary has request/gate constructs but no swap or id-binding keys. activation.fires and doesNotFire were neutralized in place the same way (hx-swap-oob → out-of-band swap construct; id={rowId} → a dynamically bound expression id); their htmx wordings remain visible in bun.json, the delivered reference example. Per rule 7, the detector/finding ids (htmx_hypermedia_detector) and the 'language' activation fact are bunOnly, while severity 2 and the strict disposition live in core:verification. The id-must-resolve-to-an-existing-element requirement stays as prefer/evidence/verification material (not a second then); bun.json's splitSuggestion (coder.htmx.swap-oob-id-resolves) is a realization-side proposal and was not promoted into the core.
